facts.fact: The Oracle Fusion Cloud EPM: Features with AI book (part G44587-23) has chapters on LLM usage, embedded AI features, EPM Agent Skills and APIs, Fusion AI EPM Assistants, EPM AI in Smart View, and 'Published REST APIs Through External AI Tools' (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/epmai/toc.htm).

EPM Agent Skills are Oracle-packaged skills for third-party AI agents; each skill bundles instructions, reference material and executable tools (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/about_epm_ai_skills.html).

EPM Agent Skills follow the Agent Skills open standard (agentskills.io), so compatible agents can reuse the same skills (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/epmai/epm_skills.html).

Download EPM Agent Skills from Settings and Actions > Downloads > 'EPM AI Skills', which saves a zip (package Epm_Agent_Skills / EPM_AGENT_SKILLS); for desktop clients ('ChatGPT/Codex and Claude') extract it into the agent's skills directory, for browser interfaces (ChatGPT, Claude) upload the zip to the skill library, and keep the folder structure intact (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/downloading_and_installing_epm_ai_skills.html).

EPM Agent Skills can be installed in ChatGPT/Codex desktop clients by extracting the zip into the skills directory, or in the ChatGPT browser interface by uploading the zip to the skill library (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/downloading_and_installing_epm_ai_skills.html).

EPM Agent Skills can be installed in the Claude desktop client by extracting the zip into the skills directory, or in the Claude browser interface by uploading the zip to the skill library (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/downloading_and_installing_epm_ai_skills.html).

From the November 2026 (26.11) update, the 'EPM AI Skills' download appears only after a Cloud EPM or Cloud EDM business process has been created in the environment (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-nov26/26nov-epm-wn-t79512.htm).

In EPM Agent Skills a root router (EPM Skill Routing) sends each request to a domain folder: Auth (Shared Authentication skill), Core (11 infrastructure-administration skills) and Platform (Platform Data Exploration, plus the Strategic Modeling Data Exploration, Scenario Automation and EPS Alternatives skills) (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/epmai/ai_features_at_a_glance_skills_apis.html).

The Core folder of EPM Agent Skills holds 11 infrastructure-administration skills, announced in the 26.11 readiness notes (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-nov26/26nov-epm-wn-f52308.htm).

The Core AI skills cover access control and identity reports, environment/services/maintenance, Essbase block analysis, Essbase data export, files/Object Storage/SFTP, identity and access management, migration and snapshots, query governor, security administration, simulate concurrent usage, and user activity reports through validated REST operations (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-nov26/26nov-epm-wn-f52308.htm).

Most state-changing operations in the EPM Core AI skills require explicit user approval, and the skills honor the invoking user's EPM permissions (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-nov26/26nov-epm-wn-f52308.htm).

The Platform Data Exploration skill, new in 26.11, is part of the Platform folder of EPM Agent Skills and applies to Planning and FreeForm (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-nov26/26nov-epm-wn-f52295.htm).

The Platform Data Exploration skill reads applications, cubes/plan types, dimensions, members, forms, dashboards and selected Planning values through a packaged 'EPM Client Library' (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-nov26/26nov-epm-wn-f52295.htm).

Writes are disabled in the Platform Data Exploration skill, but form and dashboard exports can still run configured load rules, which causes server-side effects (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-nov26/26nov-epm-wn-f52295.htm).

The EPM Core and shared Auth skills need Python 3.10+, and the Planning and Strategic Modeling skills also need Node.js (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/connecting_using_basic_authentication.html).

The documented EPM Agent Skills connection is Basic auth from a private four-line config file (URL, environment name, username, password); accounts that require MFA for Basic REST auth cannot use it (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/connecting_using_basic_authentication.html).

The bootstrap script Auth\scripts\epm_auth.py bootstrap --basic-config-file <file> writes an environments.json session registry under %LOCALAPPDATA%\OracleEPM\ (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/connecting_using_basic_authentication.html).

The EPM Agent Skills package ships 22 OpenAPI-style YAML definitions, for example epm-pbcs-jobs-api.yaml, epm-pbcs-dimensions-api.yaml, epm-pbcs-insights-api.yaml, epm-pbcs-service-connections-api.yaml and strategic-modeling-openapi.yaml (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/epmai/ai_features_at_a_glance_skills_apis.html).

Oracle says the APIs defined in the EPM Agent Skills YAML files 'will later be documented in the REST APIs guide' (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/epmai/ai_features_at_a_glance_skills_apis.html).

EPM Assistants are agent teams built in Oracle Fusion AI Agent Studio; agents are imported from JSON and call Cloud EPM REST APIs, scoped to each user's EPM roles (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/downloading_epm_assistants.html).
EPM Assistants call Cloud EPM REST APIs scoped to each user's EPM roles (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/downloading_epm_assistants.html).

Download EPM Assistants as EPM_AI_Agent_Artifacts-<APP>-<SERVICE>.zip from Downloads > 'EPM Assistants', import under AI Agent Studio > Monitoring and Evaluation > Supervisor Agents > Import, test with Play and Debug Play, then Publish (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/import_epm_assistants_into_oracle_fusion_ai_agent_studio.html).

The 'EPM Assistants' download option shows only for EPCM, FreeForm and Planning with AI enabled (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/downloading_epm_assistants.html).

facts.fact: The EPM Assistants catalog includes Transaction Matching Configuration Assistant (ARCS), PCM Assistant and PCM Calculation Assistant (EPCM), Consolidation Approvals Assistant and Data Retrieval Diagnosis Assistant (FCCS), Narrative Reporting Assistant, Tax Journal Assistant, IPM Insights Assistant, EPM Activity Reports Assistant, and Task Manager Assistants (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/epmai/ai_features_at_a_glance_fusion_ai.html).
All EPM Assistants are GenAI agents that require AI Agent Studio (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/epmai/ai_features_at_a_glance_fusion_ai.html).

Several EPM Assistants (IPM Insights, PCM, Configurable Consolidation Rules, Data Retrieval Diagnosis, Transaction Matching Configuration) were announced in the 26.10 and 26.11 readiness notes (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-nov26/26nov-epm-wn-t79416.htm).
EPM Assistants use the LLMs that AI Agent Studio offers (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/epmai/llm_availability_and_usage_in_epm.html).

EPM-specific LLM features outside Agent Studio, including the in-product UI features, point to the OCI Generative AI GPT-OSS model documentation (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/epmai/llm_availability_and_usage_in_epm.html).

The GPT-OSS model referenced by EPM LLM features is documented under OCI Generative AI (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/epmai/llm_availability_and_usage_in_epm.html).

Cloud EPM environments not on 26.08 or later by the end of January 2027 lose access to Generative AI features (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-nov26/26nov-epm-wn-t79512.htm).

facts.fact: EPM Skills for Oracle Digital Assistant (ODA), the older conversational channel, are de-supported in November 2026 (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-nov26/26nov-epm-wn-t79512.htm).

facts.target: EPM Skills for Oracle Digital Assistant
facts.fact: Oracle points to Oracle AI for Fusion Applications instead of the de-supported EPM Skills for Oracle Digital Assistant (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-nov26/26nov-epm-wn-t79512.htm).
Predictive Planning is a Planning predictive AI feature first released in 16.12 (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/planning-budgeting-cloud/pfusu/ai_features_for_planning.html).
Auto Predict (scheduled prediction jobs) is a Planning AI feature first released in 20.08 (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/planning-budgeting-cloud/pfusu/ai_features_for_planning.html).

IPM Insights (anomalies, forecast bias and variances, with GenAI summaries) was first released for Planning in 21.11 (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/planning-budgeting-cloud/pfusu/ai_features_for_planning.html).
Bring Your Own ML (PMML models) is a Planning AI feature first released in 21.11 (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/planning-budgeting-cloud/pfusu/ai_features_for_planning.html).
Predictive Cash Forecasting is a Planning AI feature first released in 24.04 (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/planning-budgeting-cloud/pfusu/ai_features_for_planning.html).
Advanced Predictions (multivariate ML forecasts) is a Planning AI feature first released in 25.08 (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/planning-budgeting-cloud/pfusu/ai_features_for_planning.html).
Reporting Agent (GenAI Q&A over report grids) is a Planning AI feature first released in 26.07 (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/planning-budgeting-cloud/pfusu/ai_features_for_planning.html).
IPM Insights is supported for EPCM, FCCS, FreeForm, Planning and Tax Reporting, and in Smart View (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/planning-budgeting-cloud/pfusu/ai_working_with_ipm.html).

26.11 added IPM Insights Analysis, top insights in dashboards, insights viewed from forms and dashboards, a REST API for Planning insight details, and the IPM-Manage granular role (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-nov26/26nov-epm-wn-t79416.htm).
The IPM-Manage granular role for IPM Insights was added in 26.11 (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-nov26/26nov-epm-wn-t79416.htm).

EPM Automate autoPredict and dismissIPMInsights script the Planning predictive features from the CLI (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cepma/epm_automate_command_links_pbcs.html).

Groovy rules can build calc scripts at runtime, validate and cancel saves, and run rules, rulesets and templates synchronously; they run in Planning (including modules, Sales Planning, SWP and Cash Forecasting), EPCM, FCCS, FreeForm and Tax Reporting (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/planning-budgeting-cloud/pfusa/creating_a_groovy_rule_about.html).
Groovy rules need EPM Enterprise Cloud Service, Enterprise PBCS or PBCS Plus One (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/planning-budgeting-cloud/pfusa/creating_a_groovy_rule_about.html).
Groovy rules are not supported in composite forms (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/planning-budgeting-cloud/pfusa/creating_a_groovy_rule_about.html).

In Groovy, getEPMAutomate() returns an EpmAutomate instance that runs EPM Automate commands with no client install (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cepma/epm_auto_groovy_methods.html).

Server-side EPM Automate from Groovy runs every command except downloadFile, upgrade and uploadFile, and recreate, refreshCube, replay, resetService and restructureCube cannot target the environment that is running the script (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cepma/epm_auto_groovy_supported_commands.html).

Server-side Groovy EPM Automate runs in Planning and Planning Modules (EPM Enterprise), EPBCS, PBCS Plus One, FreeForm, EPCM, FCCS (EPM Enterprise), Tax Reporting (EPM Enterprise), SWP and Sales Planning, and a script there can issue commands against any Cloud EPM environment, for example Narrative Reporting (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cepma/epm_auto_groovy_supported_env.html).

Groovy rules call external or other-EPM REST endpoints through Connections defined in Manage Connections, via the Groovy Connection API (for example operation.application.getConnection("name")); exact method names were not confirmed (unverified) (https://docs.oracle.com/cloud/latest/epm-common/GROOV/).
A future update will block Connection URLs that use IP addresses (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-nov26/26nov-epm-wn-t79512.htm).

facts.fact: From 26.08, a grid created in Groovy and not closed fails script validation, and if the rule is deployed anyway Job Console shows 'completed with warnings' (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-nov26/26nov-epm-wn-t79512.htm).

A future update aligns ASO grid suppression for DataGridDefinitionBuilder and the exportdataslice REST API with Form Designer (NON EMPTY MDX when suppressMissingRows is true) (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-nov26/26nov-epm-wn-t79512.htm).

A Data Integration Pipeline runs a series of Data Integration jobs as one process (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/diepm/integrations_pipeline_process.html).

Pipeline job types include Integration, Copy from Object Storage, Copy from SFTP and EPM Platform Job; runtime variables are supported, and non-administrators can be allowed to run Pipelines (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/diepm/integrations_pipeline_process.html).

No EPM-native RAG, vector store, agent memory or evaluation runtime is documented; the external-AI pattern makes the customer responsible for model choice, prompts, security boundaries, auditability and output review (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/epmai/published_apis_through_external_ai_tools.html).

Agent hosting, monitoring and evaluation for EPM Assistants sit in Oracle Fusion AI Agent Studio, while for EPM Agent Skills they sit in the customer's own agent (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/epmai/published_apis_through_external_ai_tools.html).

The Cloud EPM REST URL pattern is https://<BASE-URL>/<context>/rest/{api_version}/{path}, where <BASE-URL> is the service URL without /epmcloud (for example https://epm-acme.epm.us-phoenix-1.ocs.oraclecloud.com) (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/prest/url_structure_overview.html).

Cloud EPM REST context paths are HyperionPlanning (Planning, FCCS, Tax Reporting, EPCM; Enterprise Journal at /HyperionPlanning/rest/ej/, Supplemental Data at /HyperionPlanning/rest/sdm/), interop (Migration/LCM, identity and platform), aif (Data Integration and Data Management), armARCS (Account Reconciliation) and epm (legacy Profitability and Cost Management) (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/prest/url_structure_overview.html).

Oracle does not support any Cloud EPM REST endpoint not in the guide, nor any URL containing the path token /internal/, and a bare <BASE-URL> call fails (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/prest/url_structure_overview.html).

The Cloud EPM REST API version is part of the URL and is required; a missing or unsupported version fails and version identifiers are case sensitive (v1 works, V1 does not), yet Data Integration uses V1 (for example /aif/rest/V1/jobs) (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/prest/versioning.html).

Planning REST is v3; Migration exposes legacy 11.1.2.3.600 alongside v1 and v2, and GET /interop/rest/ lists versions with lifecycle (active or deprecated) and latest (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/prest/get_rest_api_versions_for_lcm.html).

The REST APIs for Oracle Fusion Cloud EPM guide (part G42939-13) has chapters for Infrastructure, Cloud EPM Platform, Account Reconciliation, EPCM, FCCS, Planning and FreeForm, PCM, Tax Reporting, Identity Domains, Narrative Reporting and EDM REST APIs (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/prest/toc.htm).

Planning jobs are submitted with POST /HyperionPlanning/rest/v3/applications/{app}/jobs and body {"jobType","jobName","parameters"}; the job must already be defined in the application, and record counts and errors come from GET .../jobs/{jobId}/details with offset and limit (default 25) (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/prest/execute_a_job.html).

A Planning job response returns jobID and a numeric status: -1 in progress, 0 success, 1 error, 2 cancel pending, 3 cancelled, 4 invalid parameter; poll until status is not -1 (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/prest/retrieve_job_status_details.html).

POST /aif/rest/V1/jobs with jobType INTEGRATION runs a Data Integration integration (recommended over the older DATARULE type), and jobType PIPELINE with jobName set to the Pipeline code and a variables map (for example STARTPERIOD, ENDPERIOD, IMPORTMODE, EXPORTMODE, SEND_MAIL) runs a Pipeline (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/prest/fdmee_run_pipeline.html).

Poll Data Integration jobs with GET /aif/rest/V1/jobs/{jobId} (status codes as for Planning; jobStatus for example SUCCESS, plus logFileName and outputFileName) (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/prest/fdmee_jobstatus_di.html).

Running Pipelines via the Data Integration REST API needs the Service Administrator role (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/prest/fdmee_run_pipeline.html).

facts.fact: Migration (LCM) v2 export is POST /interop/rest/v2/snapshots/export with {"snapshotName":...}, returning status -1 and a 'Job Status' link; poll GET /interop/rest/v2/status/migration/{jobId}, and task details are at .../{jobId}/{taskId}/details?msgtype=error|warn|info (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/prest/lcm_export_v2.html).

facts.target: Cloud EPM Migrations - Administer granular role
facts.fact: Migration v2 snapshot export requires Service Administrator or the Migrations - Administer granular role (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/prest/lcm_export_v2.html).
The Migration v2 export doc says a completed job returns 1 but its example shows 0 (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/prest/lcm_export_v2.html).

Chunked file and snapshot upload (v2): POST /interop/rest/v2/files/upload with {fileName,fileSize} to get a job ID, then PATCH /interop/rest/v2/files/upload/{jobId} with Content-Type: application/octet-stream and a Chunk-Range: <start>-<end> header, then POST .../{jobId}/complete to extract, then poll GET /interop/rest/v2/status/jobs/{jobId} (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/prest/upload_application_snapshot_v2.html).

Migration REST covers list and restore backups (v2), LCM import and export (v2), and rename, upload, download and copy snapshot (v1 and v2); v2 adds artifact categories, incremental category exports, updated-artifact lists, snapshot modification history, selective artifact import, import options and migration status (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/prest/lcm_rest_apis.html).

Copy Snapshot over REST needs the source password encrypted with the EPM Automate encrypt command (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/prest/lcm_rest_apis.html).

Add Users to an Identity Domain comes in v1 (CSV uploaded first with the Upload API) and v2 (JSON payload); it creates accounts only (existing users are untouched), and resetpassword=true sends credential emails (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/prest/lcm_add_user_parent.html).

facts.target: OCI IAM Identity Domain Administrator role
facts.fact: The Add Users to an Identity Domain REST API needs Identity Domain Administrator plus an application role (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/prest/lcm_add_user_parent.html).
26.11 added 141 new Cloud EPM Platform REST APIs for Planning and FreeForm (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-nov26/26nov-epm-wn-f52441.htm).

The 26.11 Platform REST APIs cover applications (including an AI-focused markdown 'Get Application Summary'), cubes, dimensions and members, Calculation Manager rule and ruleset CRUD, validate and deploy, form and dashboard definitions, data export/import (including ad hoc, slice and MDX export), jobs, approval units, substitution and user variables, user preferences, Business Concepts and Semantic Foundation, Insights, IPM calendar, and service connections (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-nov26/26nov-epm-wn-f52441.htm).

The Cloud EPM Platform REST APIs are part of the Cloud EPM REST APIs for Planning and FreeForm (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/epmai/published_apis_through_external_ai_tools.html).

The 26.11 Connections REST APIs create, get, update and delete connections for EPM, NetSuite, Oracle Fusion Apps and Other Web Service Providers, with OAuth 2.0 where supported, for Planning, FreeForm, FCCS and Tax Reporting (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-nov26/26nov-epm-wn-f52254.htm).
Credentials are excluded from Connections REST API GET responses (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-nov26/26nov-epm-wn-f52254.htm).
The Connections REST APIs manage connections to NetSuite (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-nov26/26nov-epm-wn-f52254.htm).
The Connections REST APIs manage connections to Oracle Fusion Apps (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-nov26/26nov-epm-wn-f52254.htm).

All Cloud EPM REST requests need auth; Basic auth goes in the Authorization header, and Oracle recommends OAuth 2 over Basic (25.11 notice) but gives no Basic-auth retirement date (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2025/epm-nov25/25nov-epm-wn-f42020.htm).

OAuth 2 for Cloud EPM REST (OCI Gen 2 environments only) sends Authorization: Bearer <access token> (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/prest/authentication.html).
Users set up for Basic auth with MFA cannot call the Cloud EPM REST APIs (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/prest/authentication.html).

The documented Cloud EPM OAuth flow is Device Code plus Refresh Token against the IAM identity domain (/oauth2/v1/device, /oauth2/v1/token) with scope urn:opc:serviceInstanceID=<ID>urn:opc:resource:consumer::all offline_access; Authorization Code, Resource Owner Password and Assertion also work, but client credentials is not documented for EPM REST (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/prest/authentication_oath.html).

Cloud EPM access tokens last about 3600 s; refresh tokens are single-use and expire after 7 days unused (refresh at least every 6 days), each script needs its own refresh token, and tokens are per environment (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/prest/authentication_oath.html).

From 26.11, EPM Automate login and the REST APIs reject usernames prefixed with the cloud account name (for example acct.user@example.com); supply the plain username (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-nov26/26nov-epm-wn-f52345.htm).

From 26.11, EPM Automate login rejects usernames prefixed with the cloud account name (for example acct.user@example.com) (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-nov26/26nov-epm-wn-f52345.htm).

Oracle publishes no language SDK for EPM REST; integration is raw HTTP plus EPM Automate (unverified) (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/epmai/published_apis_through_external_ai_tools.html).

The only Oracle-packaged client code found for EPM REST is the 'EPM Client Library' and scripts inside the EPM Agent Skills package (unverified) (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/epmai/published_apis_through_external_ai_tools.html).

facts.fact: There is no official EPM MCP server: Oracle's official MCP repository (github.com/oracle/mcp) lists OCI, database, MySQL, GoldenGate and similar servers, none for EPM or Fusion EPM, and MCP does not appear in the Features with AI guide (https://github.com/oracle/mcp/tree/main/src).
Oracle's official MCP repository github.com/oracle/mcp lists OCI, database, MySQL, GoldenGate and similar MCP servers (https://github.com/oracle/mcp/tree/main/src).

Oracle's chosen channels for AI agents on EPM are EPM Agent Skills (Agent Skills standard) and EPM Assistants in AI Agent Studio, not MCP (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/epmai/toc.htm).
No community EPM MCP server was verified because the web-search budget ran out before GitHub or npm could be searched (unverified) (https://github.com/oracle/mcp).

Oracle Fusion Cloud EPM and EDM can be reached through API gateways and reverse proxies such as Google Apigee and IBM DataPower (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/epmai/published_apis_through_external_ai_tools.html).

IBM DataPower is a supported API gateway or reverse proxy in front of Cloud EPM and EDM (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/epmai/published_apis_through_external_ai_tools.html).

The EPM Integration Agent runs a query against an on-premises relational source, or a Jython, Groovy or Java script for other sources such as third-party REST, and loads the result into Cloud EPM; its prepackaged adapters include write-back (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/diepm/epm_agent_tile_104x84710842.html).

The EPM Integration Agent runs in synchronous mode (Cloud EPM calls the agent through a web-server gateway) or asynchronous mode (the agent polls Cloud EPM for queued jobs), and agents are grouped into clusters (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/diepm/epm_agent_epm_zip_102x805297a3.html).

Download EPMAgent.zip, run createAppFolder.bat, and configure C:\EPMAgentData\config\agentparams.ini with AGENT_NAME, CLUSTER (default EPMCLUSTER), PORT, CLOUD_URL (no /epmcloud), CLOUD_USER_NAME (a native user, not SSO), CLOUD_PASSWORD (from encryptpassword.bat) and optionally CLIENT_ID for OAuth; it can run as a Windows service (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/diepm/epm_agent_config_parameter_106x805351e5.html).

EPM Integration Agent defaults are POLL_INTERVAL 120 s, EXECUTION_POOL_SIZE 2, FILE_UPLOAD_SIZE 50 MB and AMW_IDLE_TIME 15 min (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/diepm/epm_agent_config_parameter_106x805351e5.html).

The EPM Integration Agent signs in with CLOUD_USER_NAME (a native user, not SSO) and CLOUD_PASSWORD encrypted by encryptpassword.bat (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/diepm/epm_agent_config_parameter_106x805351e5.html).

The EPM Integration Agent optionally takes a CLIENT_ID in agentparams.ini for OAuth (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/diepm/epm_agent_config_parameter_106x805351e5.html).

Prebuilt Data Integration sources: Oracle ERP Cloud (GL balances, metadata, FX rates, BI Publisher reports as ESS jobs, write-back, Budgetary Control), Fusion Project Management, Oracle HCM Cloud, NetSuite, SAP (with GL drill-through), JD Edwards, E-Business Suite, PeopleSoft GL, Autonomous Database, Account Reconciliation, and an incremental file adapter (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/diepm/toc.htm).

Data Integration's Oracle ERP Cloud source covers GL balances, metadata, FX rates, BI Publisher reports as ESS jobs, write-back, and Budgetary Control (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/diepm/toc.htm).
Data Integration has a prebuilt SAP source with GL drill-through (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/diepm/toc.htm).

New customers integrate NetSuite with Cloud EPM using the NetSuite EPM Connector SuiteApp; the Sync SuiteApps add metadata loads, write-back, predefined saved searches and running EPM jobs from NetSuite (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/diepm/integrations_netsuite_intro_100xbda13a64.html).

Existing NSPB Sync customers keep NSPB Sync for NetSuite-to-EPM integration (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/diepm/integrations_netsuite_intro_100xbda13a64.html).
OAuth 2.0 support for NetSuite connections in Cloud EPM arrived in 26.10 and 26.11 (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-nov26/26nov-epm-wn-t79416.htm).

From 26.10, EPM calls Fusion Applications REST over OAuth 2.0: generate a certificate and key, create an EPM Trusted Client Application, then configure a Fusion ERP connection in EPM Connections, giving server-to-server calls that preserve user identity (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-oct26/26oct-epm-wn-f51820.htm).

26.11 adds an 'Oracle Fusion Application Cloud Provider' connection type and OAuth 2.0 for cross-environment connections (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-nov26/26nov-epm-wn-t79416.htm).

AI Agent Studio to EPM authentication is set up under Credentials > Data Source Applications using a confidential application in the EPM identity domain with an uploaded public certificate and private key (PEM), a scope, the EPM base URL and the IDCS URL (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/establish_a_data_source_connection_in_ai_agent_studio.html).

SSO between Agent Studio and EPM must be in place first, and the data source name must exactly match the suffix after EPM_AI_Agent_Artifacts- (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/establish_a_data_source_connection_in_ai_agent_studio.html).

Smart View for Office (the Excel, Word and PowerPoint client) version 26.200 is listed in 26.11 and adds IPM Insights for forms, reports in PowerPoint and member-search improvements (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-nov26/26nov-epm-wn-f52148.htm).

Download Smart View from My Oracle Support or Oracle Technical Resources, or via Downloading and Installing Clients (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-nov26/26nov-epm-wn-f52148.htm).

facts.fact: Events, webhooks, JDBC and GraphQL are not documented for Cloud EPM; integration is pull-based (REST, EPM Automate, scheduled jobs and Pipelines) or file-based (inbox/outbox, Object Storage and SFTP copy commands) (unverified) (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/prest/toc.htm).

EPM Automate is the official Cloud EPM CLI, documented in Oracle Fusion Cloud EPM: Working with EPM Automate (part G45306-09) (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cepma/).

There is no winget or MSI feed for EPM Automate; in an environment open Settings and Actions > Downloads > EPM Automate > 'Download for Windows', then run EPM Automate.exe as administrator (Windows Administrators group required) (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cepma/installing_epm_automate_windows.html).

EPM Automate installs to C:\Program Files\Oracle\EPM Automate on Windows, and the optional EPMAUTOMATE_BASE_DIR environment variable sets the session file directory (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cepma/installing_epm_automate_windows.html).

From 26.04, EPM Automate runtime data on Windows (logs, .epw password files, downloads, preferences) defaults to C:\ProgramData\Oracle\EPM Automate; scripts that use relative paths for uploadFile sources or .epw files must have those files there, and users must sign in again after upgrade (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-apr26/26apr-epm-wn-f44316.htm).

The EPM Automate Windows installer bundles the JRE, while Linux, UNIX and macOS need a separate JDK; from 26.10 the Linux/UNIX client uses JDK 21 via JAVA_HOME (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cepma/installing_epm_automate_jre.html).
JDK 17 still works for EPM Automate but is deprecated in 27.01 (January 2027) (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-nov26/26nov-epm-wn-t79512.htm).

epmautomate login USERNAME PASSWORD|PASSWORD_FILE.epw BASE_URL [ProxyServerUserName=] [ProxyServerPassword=] [ProxyServerDomain=] signs in; -p <paramfile> passes values from a file, and a plain-text password triggers a warning (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cepma/epm_auto_login.html).

EPM Automate command and parameter names are case-insensitive, but mandatory parameters are positional (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cepma/epm_automate_command_usage.html).

Run epmautomate encrypt REFRESH_TOKEN ENCRYPTION_KEY FILE.epw ClientID=CLIENT_ID, then login with that .epw (the username is then ignored); do not sign in with an OAuth refresh token to run addUsers, removeUsers, assignRole or unassignRole, and basic auth keeps working when OAuth is enabled (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cepma/epm_automate_oauth.html).

EPM Automate changed the .epw format in 26.09; environments on 26.09 to 26.11 accept both formats, and from 26.12 only the new format works, so clients older than 26.09 fail and must upgrade to 26.09 or later and re-run encrypt (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-nov26/26nov-epm-wn-t79512.htm).
The EPM Integration Agent should keep an .epw from 26.08 or earlier until the agent is on 26.10 (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-nov26/26nov-epm-wn-t79512.htm).

EPM Automate data and metadata commands: importData, exportData, importMetadata, exportMetadata, exportEssbaseData, clearCube, refreshCube, restructureCube, compactCube, mergeDataSlices, executeAggregationProcess, importValidIntersections/exportValidIntersections, getSubstVar/setSubstVars, sortMember (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cepma/epm_automate_command_links_pbcs.html).

EPM Automate job and integration commands: runBusinessRule (for example epmautomate runBusinessRule RollupUSSales Period=Q1 Entity=USA), runRuleSet, runPlanTypeMap, runIntegration (replaces the deprecated runDataRule), runBatch, runPipeline PIPELINE_CODE [VAR=VALUE], importMapping/exportMapping, runDMReport, exportJobConsole (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cepma/epm_auto_run_integration.html).
The EPM Automate runPipeline PIPELINE_CODE [VAR=VALUE] command was added in 25.02 (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2025/epm-feb25/25feb-epm-wn-f37033.htm).

EPM Automate snapshot, backup and environment commands: exportSnapshot, importSnapshot, copySnapshotFromInstance, renameSnapshot, listBackups, restoreBackup, cloneEnvironment, restoreEnvironment, recreate, resetService, runDailyMaintenance, getDailyMaintenanceStartTime/setDailyMaintenanceStartTime, skipUpdate, upgrade (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cepma/epm_automate_command_links_pbcs.html).

EPM Automate file and report commands: uploadFile, downloadFile, listFiles, deleteFile, deleteFolder, copyFileFromInstance, copyToObjectStorage/copyFromObjectStorage, copyToSFTP/copyFromSFTP, executeReportBurstingDefinition, exportLibraryDocument/importLibraryDocument, runTaskManagerReport, sendMail, plus replay and simulateConcurrentUsage for load testing (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cepma/epm_automate_command_links_pbcs.html).

EPM Automate adds local-machine operations (uploadFile and downloadFile from a client disk, encrypt for .epw files, upgrade of itself) and replay of HAR traffic, while REST is needed for things EPM Automate lacks, such as job details paging and the 26.11 Platform APIs for dimension, form, dashboard and rule CRUD (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-nov26/26nov-epm-wn-f52441.htm).

Copy Snapshot over REST still needs an EPM Automate-encrypted password, and Groovy server-side EPM Automate cannot run uploadFile, downloadFile or upgrade (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/prest/lcm_rest_apis.html).

The EPM Automate client is versioned with the monthly update (for example 26.09 and later required for the new .epw format) and is updated with epmautomate upgrade; no exact current build number was confirmed for 2026-11-14 (unverified) (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cepma/epm_auto_upgrade.html).

The EPM Integration Agent is an official Cloud EPM client shipped as EPMAgent.zip that runs as a Java process or Windows service (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/diepm/epm_agent_epm_zip_102x805297a3.html).
Smart View for Office 26.200 is one of the official Cloud EPM clients (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-nov26/26nov-epm-wn-f52148.htm).

The EPM Agent Skills package is an official Cloud EPM client consisting of Python 3.10+ and Node.js scripts (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/connecting_using_basic_authentication.html).

There is no Oracle Terraform provider for EPM application content; configuration is promoted as snapshots (Migration/LCM export and import, exportSnapshot/importSnapshot) and scripted with EPM Automate or REST, which is the practical 'configuration as code' path (unverified) (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/prest/lcm_rest_apis.html).

The Cloud EPM docs root (Get Started) at https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/epm-cloud/index.html links each business process, Cloud Readiness/What's New, FAQs for Monthly Updates (.../enterprise-performance-management-common/epmfq/), AI Features and Cloud EPM Platform (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/epm-cloud/index.html).
The REST API reference is REST APIs for Oracle Fusion Cloud EPM, with the TOC at prest/toc.htm (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/prest/).
The EPM Automate guide is Working with EPM Automate (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cepma/).
The Features with AI guide covers Agent Skills, EPM Assistants and AI in Smart View (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/epmai/).

The Administering Data Integration guide covers Pipelines, the EPM Integration Agent and source adapters (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/diepm/toc.htm).

The Getting Started Guide for Administrators (cgsad) covers OAuth, daily maintenance, backups, EPM Assistants and Agent Skills setup (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/getting_started_with_epm_ai_skills.html).
The Oracle Fusion Cloud EPM Groovy Scripting Reference (Javadoc) has identifier E96254-40 (https://docs.oracle.com/cloud/latest/epm-common/GROOV/).

Oracle's official MCP repository, which has no EPM server, is at github.com/oracle/mcp (https://github.com/oracle/mcp).
No EPM-specific public status page was confirmed (unverified) (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/epm-cloud/index.html).

Cloud EPM monthly updates apply to test first and production two weeks later, in the first daily maintenance at or after 22:00 UTC (14:00 UTC for the OC4 and OC19 realms) on a Friday; for 26.11, test environments updated Friday 2026-11-06 and production Friday 2026-11-20 (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-nov26/26nov-epm-wn-f52029.htm).

epmautomate skipUpdate add version=YY.MM comment="..." (Service Administrator) skips a monthly update, one version per command, and remove clears all skips (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cepma/epm_auto_skip_update.html).

skipUpdate skips at most three monthly updates within three months of the current one; weekly and emergency patches still apply, skipping is not allowed on a one-off patch, and if test and production skip differently snapshot migration between them may not be supported (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cepma/epm_auto_skip_update.html).

Off-mainline policy (26.11, effective immediately): an environment can stay on a one-off patch, or on Skip Update, for up to three months, with one Oracle-approved extension to six months in total (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-nov26/26nov-epm-wn-f52344.htm).

Daily maintenance reserves one hour; if unset, the default start is random between 22:00 and 01:00 in the hosting region's local time, changeable with setDailyMaintenanceStartTime or the REST v2 API; users get a warning 15 minutes ahead and are logged off with unsaved data lost (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/6_house_keeping_tasks_daily_maintenance_tasks.html).

Jobs started from EPM Automate, REST or Job Console schedules are restricted during the maintenance window for Planning, EPCM, FCCS and Tax Reporting, and Data Integration, import/export and refresh can stay unavailable shortly after restart (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/6_house_keeping_tasks_daily_maintenance_tasks.html).

Asynchronous EPM Integration Agents idle for AMW_IDLE_TIME (default and minimum 15 minutes) during automated or unscheduled maintenance (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/diepm/epm_agent_config_parameter_106x805351e5.html).

Daily maintenance creates an 'Artifact Snapshot' and an environment backup; on OCI Gen 2 backups are kept 60 days in Object Storage (list with listBackups, restore with restoreBackup), and if snapshots total more than 150 GB the oldest are deleted (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/backup_and_disaster_recovery_faq.html).
Oracle recommends downloading the daily Cloud EPM snapshot (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/epmss/about_epm_snapshots.html).

Cloud EPM web-interface uploads are capped at 2 GB for snapshots and 500 MB for other files; use EPM Automate uploadFile for larger files, and downloads have no size limit (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/tsepm/8_troubleshoot_data_export_import_file_size.html).

The EPM Integration Agent uploads in 50 MB chunks by default (FILE_UPLOAD_SIZE) (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/diepm/epm_agent_config_parameter_106x805351e5.html).

The Cloud EPM REST status-code page lists 200, 201, 202, 400, 401, 403, 404, 405, 406, 415, 500 and 503 ('temporary overloading or maintenance') and documents no 429 code, Retry-After header, rate limit or concurrency quota; treat 503 as retryable and serialize heavy jobs (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/prest/status_codes.html).

EPM provides simulateConcurrentUsage and replay (EPM Automate and REST) for load testing, and parallel simulateConcurrentUsage runs are supported from 26.11 (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-nov26/26nov-epm-wn-t79416.htm).

facts.fact: Cloud EPM refresh tokens are single-use, rotate and expire after 7 days idle; sharing one refresh token across scripts causes 'token already consumed' errors, and tokens are per environment, so test and production need separate tokens (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/prest/authentication_oath.html).

REST calls fail for users with Basic auth plus MFA; use OAuth 2, or a native account for EPM Automate, Integration Agent and Agent Skills (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/prest/authentication.html).

The EPM Integration Agent's CLOUD_USER_NAME must be a native, non-SSO admin (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/diepm/epm_agent_config_parameter_106x805351e5.html).

Recent Cloud EPM breaking changes: 26.04 trims trailing Unicode whitespace from member names and snapshot import fails on Essbase reserved words; 26.11 removes account-name username prefixes; 26.12 rejects legacy .epw files; 27.01 deprecates JDK 17 for EPM Automate (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-nov26/26nov-epm-wn-t79512.htm).
Financial Reporting stops working in Cloud EPM in 27.02 (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-nov26/26nov-epm-wn-t79512.htm).

Oracle states that 'Data Integration will eventually replace Data Management once there is full parity between the features'; no retirement date is given (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/diepm/integrations_about_110x65a03764.html).
Data Integration REST still uses the /aif context (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/diepm/integrations_about_110x65a03764.html).
The EPM Automate runIntegration command deprecates runDataRule (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cepma/epm_auto_run_integration.html).

Current guides use 'Oracle Fusion Cloud EPM' (for example 'REST APIs for Oracle Fusion Cloud EPM') in place of 'EPM Cloud'; older URLs under /en/cloud/saas/epm-cloud/prest/ still resolve with 'EPM Cloud' titles, and the rebrand date was not confirmed (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/prest/).

facts.source: EPM Skills for Oracle Digital Assistant
facts.fact: EPM Skills for ODA are retired (de-supported November 2026) (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-nov26/26nov-epm-wn-t79512.htm).
In Account Reconciliation, 'Data Loads' became 'Balance Loads' in 26.10 (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-nov26/26nov-epm-wn-t79512.htm).
In Account Reconciliation, 'Invalid Mappings' became 'Missing Profiles' in 26.10 (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-nov26/26nov-epm-wn-t79512.htm).

The original PCM Agent and PCM Agent Performance Assistant are decommissioned in favor of the enhanced PCM Agent (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-nov26/26nov-epm-wn-t79512.htm).

Help Center documentation updates trail the readiness documents by about one week, so new-feature doc links in readiness notes may 404 at first (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-nov26/26nov-epm-wn-t79416.htm).

Unconfirmed: no official REST rate limit, concurrency cap or 429 behavior was found; confirm with Oracle Support or in the tenant before designing parallel agent workloads (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/prest/status_codes.html).

Unconfirmed: the exact Groovy Connection API class and method signatures (getConnection, get/post, and so on) for REST from Groovy, because the Javadoc pages are framesets that would not render (https://docs.oracle.com/cloud/latest/epm-common/GROOV/).

Unconfirmed: EPM Agent Skills auth beyond Basic (OAuth) and their first release date; the 26.11 readiness notes describe 'new' skills, and an earlier introduction may exist (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/connecting_using_basic_authentication.html).
Unconfirmed: no community EPM MCP servers were verified, because the web-search budget ran out before GitHub and npm were searched (https://github.com/oracle/mcp).

Unconfirmed: the maximum chunk size for REST v2 file upload is not stated on the official page; one search snippet said 50 MB (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/prest/upload_application_snapshot_v2.html).

Unconfirmed: the current EPM Automate build number for 2026-11-14 and a public Cloud EPM status page URL (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cepma/epm_auto_upgrade.html).

Unconfirmed: whether EPM-only customers (without Fusion Applications) can get AI Agent Studio to run EPM Assistants is not stated in the EPM docs (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/using_ai_agents_for_cloud_epm.html).
